name: MyFrank
description: B2B SaaS that gamifies Google review collection per employee (QR codes, challenges, multi-location tracking). For sale per founder note.

mentions.evidence: ~$10.6k MRR, 180 active subscriptions, ~$5.7k L30, ~$68.6k all-time, founded Jun 2025. Last sync Sep 29, 2026.
mentions.indieAngle: Solo-plausible local-SEO wedge — sell to franchise/multi-location ops, not to consumers.

whyItPrints: Multi-site hospitality/retail already buys review tools; attributing reviews to staff is a sticky ops wedge.
whyThisMatters:
French tool for Google reviews. What they lead with is reviews per employee, not "get more stars" as a vague promise. A shop can see which person a review belongs to, then run challenges so the staff treats it like a score. Otherwise it becomes a Sunday chore for the owner.

There's a free trial, and they say there's no commitment. You can book a call or ask for a free look at the shop. That's a pitch at a business, not at someone who wants to leave one review. Each person gets a way to collect reviews, and it works across locations, so the customer is a group of shops, not one counter.

They don't talk about the tech. They talk about the score per person, the challenges, and the trial. The founder has put the product up for sale. The site is still selling the same thing: staff-level review tracking for businesses that live off a Google rating.

A QR code and a challenge are how the employee actually collects the review. The owner sees who brought it in, and that works across more than one shop.
